app.title: Lunar Window
app.subtitle: Lunar South Pole Landing Site Navigator
app.tagline: Pick a lunar south pole site and see when the Sun and Earth rise and set there, with the terrain checked against NASA data.

common.empty_no_precomputed: No precomputed data for this point

map.title: South Pole Polar Stereographic Map
map.description: Stereographic map centered on the lunar South Pole showing candidate sites and terrain.
map.live_summary: Selected site: {name}, Latitude {lat}, Longitude {lon}. LOLA sunlight: {sun}, Earth visibility: {earth}.

dome.title: Sky Dome
dome.description: Local horizontal dome projection showing Sun and Earth paths against terrain horizon.
dome.method_note: Visibility determined when body elevation exceeds terrain horizon elevation at that azimuth.
dome.live_summary: Epoch {time}: Sun is {sun_status} (elevation {sun_el}), Earth is {earth_status} (elevation {earth_el}). Next sunset in {sunset}, next earthset in {earthset}.

verify.title: Verification Panel
verify.description: Verification table comparing model outputs against external ephemeris and data products.
verify.l1a_note: L1(a) is an implementation consistency check, not an external truth validation.
verify.l1b_title: Terrain model vs LOLA average visibility maps
verify.map_values_title: LOLA map values read at sites (no terrain model in this build)
verify.l1b_note: L1(b) compares our terrain model with NASA maps that are model outputs too. It checks the implementation and is not a comparison with real sunlight.
verify.m1_note: M1 compares the model with real LROC photographs at points near the pole. The observed lit or shadow state comes from one brightness cut per frame, so this is a consistency check with stated limits.
verify.m1_year_title: Share of a year in sunlight, LROC vs model
verify.l2_title: Best point per region and a 5 day shift of the landing date
verify.l2_note: Region positions are read from a NASA 2024 map picture and the 15 x 15 km region box is assumed from a NASA 2022 description, so both are approximate.
verify.dsn_note: The 10 degree station elevation limit is an example value, not a DSN requirement. Earth above the horizon is only an upper bound for a usable link.
verify.scope_note: Sun and Earth directions come from SPICE. Orientation and libration of the Moon use DE440 and the Moon principal axis (PA) frame. The horizon at each region comes from LOLA terrain.

timeline.title: Timeline Bar
timeline.description: Upcoming visibility intervals for selected site.
timeline.live_summary: Timeline for {site} over {range}: Sun {sun_pct}%, Earth {earth_pct}%, Both {both_pct}%.

compare.title: 3-Site Comparison and Date Shift
compare.description: Compare illumination and visibility across 3 candidate sites with base date shift.
compare.rank_swapped: Rank changed: {count} pair(s) swapped compared to baseline.
compare.live_summary: Comparison with shift {shift} days. Top site: {top_site} (Sunlight {sun_pct}%).
compare.rank_of: Only the {total} pairs among the 3 sites you picked. For all region pairs see the best point view.

footer.data_source_note: Data sources: NASA Horizons ephemerides, LOLA elevation and illumination products, LROC imagery.
footer.unofficial_disclaimer: Unofficial challenge entry for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.

m1.title: M1: check against LROC photographs
m1.description: {frames} LROC wide angle camera frames compared with the terrain shadow model at {points} points within 2 degrees of the pole.
m1.target_line: Target set at hackathon start: {pct}% or more
m1.baseline_note: Same check with a flat horizon
m1.year: Share of a year in sunlight
m1.year_note: Mean absolute difference at {n} points, correlation {r}
m1.chart_label: Agreement per frame for {frames} frames, model and flat horizon
m1.live_summary: Agreement {agreement}% over {frames} frames, {baseline}% without terrain, kappa {kappa}.

l2.title: Best point and windows inside a region
l2.description: Search a 7 by 7 grid (2 km steps) around the region point for the spot with the most hours of Sun and Earth together, then see landing dates, the longest shadow and DSN windows there.
l2.empty_site: No precomputed region data for this point.
l2.grid_label: Hours with Sun and Earth both visible for each grid point in {name}
l2.grid_note: Grid steps are {step} km in the map plane. The cross marks the region point. Numbers are hours of Sun and Earth together.
l2.best_line: {name}: point {point} has {best} h of Sun and Earth together in {period}, against {center} h at the region point (+{gain} h).
l2.approx_note: The region position is read from a public map picture and is approximate.
l2.calendar_label: Landing dates that meet the example condition, shown as marks over two years
l2.calendar_count: {n} of {total} landing dates keep the Sun up for {x} h in a row with Earth visible for at least {y}% of that time.
l2.example_note: The values {x} h and {y}% are examples, not mission requirements.
l2.flip_line: Shifting the landing date by {shift} days flipped the order of {a} of {b} region pairs and changed the top region on {c} of {d} dates.
l2.shadow_desc: Longest stretch with the Sun disc fully hidden, at the best point and at the region point.
l2.col_sens: If half the disc counts as shadow
l2.dsn_desc: Times when the Moon is at least {deg} degrees above the horizon at each station. The 10 degree limit is an example value.
l2.dsn_fraction: At the best point Earth is visible {earth}% of the time and a station can also see the Moon {comm}% of the time. Earth above the horizon is only an upper bound for a usable link.
l2.live_summary: {name}: best point {point}, +{gain} h of Sun and Earth together compared with the region point.
